topics.title: U.S. war history and White House
U.S. Constitution and Statue of Liberty

facts.title: North America country table — source grouping
facts.text: The source table groups 23 independent countries under North America, Central America, and the Caribbean; this is retained as source-attributed regional context.

facts.title: United States — Declaration of Independence
facts.text: The source dates the U.S. Declaration of Independence to 4 July 1776; this is retained as historic source-attributed reference.

facts.title: United States — Treaty of Paris boundary
facts.text: The source identifies a 1783 peace settlement after the Revolutionary War; its incorrect Versailles label is not imported.

facts.title: George Washington — first U.S. president
facts.text: George Washington took office as the first president of the United States in 1789; this is historic office context.

facts.title: United States — fifty states
facts.text: The United States is a federal republic of 50 states; Hawaii joined the Union in 1959.

facts.title: U.S. Civil War — period and Lincoln
facts.text: The U.S. Civil War ran from 1861 to 1865, and Abraham Lincoln was president during the conflict.

facts.title: United States — World War II entry
facts.text: After the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, Congress declared war on Japan on 8 December 1941 and the United States entered World War II.

facts.title: White House — construction and first residents
facts.text: White House construction began in 1792, and President John Adams and Abigail Adams became its first residents in 1800.

facts.title: White House — official name
facts.text: Theodore Roosevelt officially gave the White House its current name in 1901.

facts.title: U.S. Constitution — historic milestones
facts.text: The source dates the U.S. Constitution to 1787, its effect to 1789, and identifies 27 amendments and the first ten amendments as the Bill of Rights; the historic reference is retained with source attribution.

facts.title: U.S. Congress — chambers
facts.text: The U.S. Congress has a House of Representatives and a Senate; the source identifies 435 House voting members and 100 senators.

facts.title: Electoral College — current majority
facts.text: The current Electoral College majority is 270 of 538 electoral votes.

facts.title: Statue of Liberty — dedication and monument status
facts.text: The Statue of Liberty was dedicated in 1886 and designated a National Monument in 1924.

facts.title: Statue of Liberty — height
facts.text: From the ground to the tip of the torch, the Statue of Liberty measures 305 feet 1 inch.

facts.title: U.S. institutional vocabulary — source reference
facts.text: The source uses Secretary of State, Secretary of the Treasury, running mate, First Lady, and State of the Union as U.S. institutional terms; the record is retained as source-attributed vocabulary.

facts.title: Martin Luther King Jr. — historic chronology
facts.text: Martin Luther King Jr. was born in 1929, delivered “I Have a Dream” at the 1963 March on Washington, received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1964, and was assassinated in 1968.

notes.title: North America source-table boundary
notes.text: The regional country list is kept only as a source-attributed table. Population, industrial, size, smallest-country, and essentializing indigenous-label lines are excluded.

notes.title: U.S. independence reference boundary
notes.text: The Columbus discovery formulation, comparative rankings, and the source’s incorrect Versailles treaty name are excluded. Remaining entries are bounded historic references.

notes.title: War and White House source boundary
notes.text: Civil War, World War II, and White House records are retained only in neutral historical scope. Alternative naming, causal simplification, and unqualified military descriptions are excluded.

notes.title: Constitution and monument source boundary
notes.text: Superlatives, unstable representative counts, current election claims, and unqualified religious-first claims are excluded. The accepted constitutional and monument facts have explicit scope.

notes.title: Institutions and civil-rights source boundary
notes.text: Current president lines, party ideology compression, naval-base security claims, and territorial language are excluded. Martin Luther King chronology is retained as verified historic biography.
